mission-001.title: The blue planet
mission-001.description: investigate the world whose surface conditions allow stable liquid water and life as we know it.
mission-001.objective: Locate Earth in the Solar System.

questions.question: Which combination best explains the presence of liquid water on Earth's surface?
alternatives: Suitable temperature and sufficient atmospheric pressure
Only its distance from the Sun

questions.question: Why is Earth's atmosphere essential to habitability?
alternatives: It maintains conditions for liquid water and life
It prevents the planet from rotating

scanData: Average surface temperature: about 15 °C
Atmosphere: mostly nitrogen and oxygen
Surface: about 71% covered by liquid water
mission-001.scientificFact: Earth is the only known world with stable surface oceans and confirmed life.

dossier.overview: Earth combines liquid water, a protective atmosphere, geological activity and a suitable temperature range.
sections: Atmosphere and environment
Atmospheric pressure and a moderate greenhouse effect help keep water liquid.
Orbit and structure
Its nearly circular orbit and rocky structure support relatively stable conditions.
Scientific exploration
Satellites monitor climate, oceans, vegetation and changes across the planet.
dossier.learnMore: Habitability depends on several interacting factors. Distance from the Sun alone is not enough: atmospheric composition, pressure, magnetic protection and long-term climate stability also matter.

mission-002.title: Traces of ancient rivers
mission-002.description: search for evidence that liquid water once flowed across the surface of a cold desert world.
mission-002.objective: Locate Mars and collect evidence of its watery past.

questions.question: Which Martian features provide strong evidence of ancient liquid water?
alternatives: An extremely strong global magnetic field
River valleys, deltas and water-altered minerals
A ring system around the planet

questions.question: Why is stable liquid water rare on the Martian surface today?
alternatives: Low pressure and cold temperatures favor freezing or evaporation
Its atmosphere is denser than Earth's

scanData: Surface: valleys, deltas and sedimentary deposits
Atmosphere: thin and dominated by carbon dioxide
Present water: mostly ice at the poles and underground
mission-002.scientificFact: Mars preserves minerals and landforms formed by water billions of years ago.

dossier.overview: Mars was once warmer and wetter. Ancient channels and deltas record environments very different from the cold desert seen today.
sections: Atmosphere and environment
A thin atmosphere produces low pressure, strong temperature changes and little protection.
Physical features
Volcanoes, canyons, impact basins and polar ice caps shape the planet.
Exploration
Orbiters, landers and rovers study rocks, climate and possible past habitability.
dossier.learnMore: Rovers have found sedimentary rocks and clay minerals that formed in water. Scientists investigate whether ancient lakes could once have supported microbial environments.

mission-003.title: The giant guardian
mission-003.description: investigate the most massive planet and the intense gravitational environment around it.
mission-003.objective: Locate Jupiter, the largest planet in the Solar System.

questions.question: Why does Jupiter strongly influence other bodies in the Solar System?
alternatives: It is the closest planet to the Sun
Its great mass creates an intense gravitational field

questions.question: Why does Jupiter lack a defined solid surface?
alternatives: It is mostly hydrogen and helium
Its surface is covered by terrestrial oceans

scanData: Mass: more than twice that of all other planets combined
Composition: mostly hydrogen and helium
Atmosphere: bands, storms and the Great Red Spot
mission-003.scientificFact: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a gigantic storm observed for centuries.

dossier.overview: Jupiter is a gas giant whose mass, rapid rotation, storms and powerful magnetic field dominate the outer Solar System.
sections: Atmosphere
Colorful bands move at different speeds and feed long-lived storms.
Physical structure
Pressure rises gradually inward; there is no ordinary solid surface.
Exploration
Spacecraft study its atmosphere, magnetosphere, rings and large family of moons.
dossier.learnMore: Jupiter can redirect comets and asteroids, but its gravity may both protect and threaten the inner planets depending on an object's trajectory.

mission-004.title: A world under pressure
mission-004.description: analyze why a planet similar in size to Earth became the hottest world in the Solar System.
mission-004.objective: Locate Venus and investigate its extreme atmosphere.

questions.question: Which Venusian characteristic traps enormous amounts of heat?
alternatives: A complete absence of atmospheric gases
A dense atmosphere rich in carbon dioxide
A rotation much faster than Earth's

questions.question: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury?
alternatives: Its extremely intense greenhouse effect retains heat

scanData: Surface temperature: about 467 °C
Atmosphere: mostly carbon dioxide
Surface pressure: about 93 times Earth's
mission-004.scientificFact: Venus is hotter than Mercury even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

dossier.overview: Venus is similar to Earth in size but its dense carbon-dioxide atmosphere created a runaway greenhouse environment.
sections: Atmosphere and environment
Thick clouds contain sulfuric acid droplets and hide the surface.
Orbit and rotation
Venus rotates very slowly and in the opposite direction to most planets.
Exploration
Radar and landers reveal volcanic plains, mountains and crushing pressure.
dossier.learnMore: Venus shows how atmospheric composition can transform a rocky planet. Studying it helps scientists understand climate evolution on Earth-sized worlds.

mission-005.title: The fastest orbit
mission-005.description: find the planet that completes the shortest journey around the Sun and experiences extreme temperatures.

questions.question: Why does Mercury have the shortest year?
alternatives: It is close to the Sun, follows a smaller orbit and moves quickly
It has the greatest number of moons
Solar gravity does not affect it
It stays still while the Sun revolves around it

questions.question: Mercury's orbital speed:
alternatives: Is greater when the planet is closer to the Sun
Falls to zero at the farthest point

scanData: Orbital period: about 88 Earth days
Surface: heavily cratered and rocky
Atmosphere: an extremely thin exosphere
mission-005.scientificFact: A solar day on Mercury lasts about 176 Earth days—twice its year.

dossier.overview: Mercury is a small rocky world close to the Sun, with a large metal core and a surface shaped by impacts.
sections: Environment
Without a thick atmosphere, daytime and nighttime temperatures differ dramatically.
Orbit
Its eccentric orbit is completed in only 88 Earth days.
Exploration
Spacecraft map its craters, magnetic field, composition and polar ice deposits.
dossier.learnMore: Despite its proximity to the Sun, permanently shadowed polar craters contain water ice because sunlight never reaches their floors.

mission-006.title: Archives of ice and rock
mission-006.description: investigate a low-density gas giant surrounded by an extraordinary system of rings.
mission-006.objective: Locate Saturn and analyze its rings and internal structure.

questions.question: What are Saturn's rings mainly made of?
alternatives: Glowing gases released by the planet
Countless particles of ice, dust and rock
Liquid water held by a lack of gravity

questions.question: What does Saturn's low average density indicate?
alternatives: Every part of the planet is empty
Its mass is distributed through a very large volume
Its rings are made of liquid water

scanData: Composition: mostly hydrogen and helium
Rings: numerous bands of ice and rocky particles
Average density: lower than liquid water
mission-006.scientificFact: Saturn's rings are enormous in width but surprisingly thin compared with their diameter.

dossier.overview: Saturn is a gas giant recognized by its broad ring system, rapid rotation and numerous moons.
sections: Atmosphere
Hydrogen, helium, clouds and storms form subtle colored bands.
Rings and structure
Ring particles range from dust grains to blocks of ice and rock.
Exploration
The Cassini mission transformed our knowledge of Saturn, its rings and moons.
dossier.learnMore: Gaps and waves in the rings reveal the gravity of moons and embedded moonlets. The system is dynamic and continues to evolve.

mission-007.title: A planet on its side
mission-007.description: the sensors detected extreme seasons on an ice giant whose rotation axis has an unusual tilt.
mission-007.objective: Find Uranus and investigate its axial tilt.

questions.question: Which consequence is associated with Uranus's extreme axial tilt?
alternatives: The planet stopped orbiting the Sun
Its poles can remain pointed toward the Sun for long periods
Its gravity disappears during part of its orbit
Its atmosphere becomes a solid surface

questions.question: Which gas helps produce Uranus's blue-green appearance?

scanData: Axial tilt: approximately 98°
Atmosphere contains hydrogen, helium and methane
Each season lasts about 21 Earth years
mission-007.scientificFact: Uranus's axis is tilted by about 98°. During parts of its long orbit, one pole points toward the Sun, producing extremely long seasons.

dossier.overview: Uranus is an ice giant whose rotation axis lies almost on its side, a feature that produces extremely long seasons.
sections: Atmosphere
Hydrogen, helium and methane are present. Methane absorbs some red light and contributes to the blue-green appearance.
Orbit and tilt
It takes about 84 years to orbit the Sun. Each season lasts approximately 21 Earth years.
Scientific exploration
Voyager 2 made the only close flyby to date; new missions have been proposed to investigate its structure and moons.
dossier.learnMore: The approximately 98° tilt may be related to major impacts or interactions early in planetary formation, but its exact origin is still under study.

mission-008.title: Winds at the limit
mission-008.description: the final investigation in this cycle seeks to understand the dynamic atmosphere of the most distant of the eight planets.
mission-008.objective: Find Neptune and analyze its atmospheric winds.

questions.question: What makes Neptune's atmosphere especially remarkable?
alternatives: It has no clouds or storms
It is made only of breathable oxygen
It has some of the fastest winds observed in the Solar System
It remains completely still because it is far from the Sun

questions.question: What helps keep Neptune's atmosphere active despite its great distance from the Sun?
alternatives: An internal source of planetary energy

scanData: Most distant of the eight planets from the Sun
Winds can exceed 2,000 km/h
Emits more energy than it receives from the Sun
mission-008.scientificFact: Even though it receives little solar energy, Neptune has a very active atmosphere, with winds that can exceed 2,000 km/h. Its internal energy helps power this activity.

dossier.overview: Neptune is the most distant of the eight planets and has a surprisingly active atmosphere, also powered by internal energy.
sections: Atmosphere and climate
Extremely fast winds and large storms are observed. Methane contributes to its blue color.
Orbit and structure
It completes one orbit in about 165 years. It is classified as an ice giant because of its internal composition.
Scientific exploration
Voyager 2 was the only probe to visit it closely, revealing rings, storms and details of Triton.
dossier.learnMore: Neptune emits more energy than it receives from the Sun. This internal flow helps sustain atmospheric motion even billions of kilometers from the system's main light source.

mission-009.title: Two worlds under the Sun
mission-009.description: compare the two planets closest to the Sun and discover why distance is not the only factor that determines temperature.
mission-009.objective: Find Mercury and Venus, in any order.

questions.question: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury?
alternatives: Because it is larger and produces its own light
Because its dense atmosphere causes an extreme greenhouse effect
Because Mercury is covered in ice
Because Venus is closer to the Sun

questions.question: Which observation demonstrates the importance of an atmosphere to temperature?
alternatives: Mercury has little atmosphere and large temperature swings; Venus retains heat with its dense atmosphere

scanData: Mercury: almost no atmosphere and large temperature swings
Venus: dense CO₂-rich atmosphere and about 467 °C
Solar distance acts together with atmospheric composition and pressure
mission-009.scientificFact: Venus demonstrates that an atmosphere can be decisive for climate: although farther from the Sun than Mercury, it is the hottest planet.

dossier.overview: Mercury and Venus receive intense solar radiation but evolved very differently. Comparing them reveals the atmosphere's role in distributing and retaining energy.
sections: Mercury
With almost no atmosphere, it alternates between extreme temperatures in illuminated and dark regions.
Venus
Its dense carbon dioxide atmosphere maintains an extreme greenhouse effect.
Scientific comparison
Proximity to the Sun, pressure and atmospheric composition must be analyzed together.
dossier.learnMore: Planetary temperature does not depend only on distance from the Sun. Reflectivity, rotation, atmospheric circulation and greenhouse gases also control the energy balance.

mission-010.title: Scales of orbital time
mission-010.description: build a comparison between inner and outer worlds to analyze how distance from the Sun influences orbital period.
mission-010.objective: Find Earth, Jupiter and Neptune, in any order.

questions.question: Which of the three planets has the longest orbital period?
Which trend appears when comparing these three planets?
alternatives: More distant planets complete orbits in less time
Distance has no relationship with period
More distant planets tend to have longer orbital periods
All travel along the same orbit

scanData: Earth: approximately 1 year per orbit
Jupiter: approximately 11.86 years per orbit
Neptune: approximately 165 years per orbit
mission-010.scientificFact: The larger the orbit, the longer its period tends to be; in addition, distant planets move more slowly on average.

dossier.overview: Earth, Jupiter and Neptune represent very different orbital scales. Their periods grow strongly as their average distance from the Sun increases.
sections: Earth
Defines the Earth year by completing its orbit in about 365 days.
Jupiter
Takes almost 12 Earth years to complete one revolution.
Neptune
Its enormous orbit requires approximately 165 Earth years.
dossier.learnMore: Kepler's third law relates the square of the orbital period to the cube of the orbit's semi-major axis. This explains why the period increases rapidly in the outer regions.

mission-011.title: The hidden planet
mission-011.description: identify a gas giant with low average density, surrounded by a broad system of ice and rock particles.
mission-011.objective: Use the clues to select the mystery planet.

questions.question: Which clue was most specific for identifying Saturn?
alternatives: Being a planet in the Solar System
Displaying a broad and visible ring system

questions.question: Saturn's rings are best described as:

scanData: Classification: gas giant
Average density lower than water
Ring system composed of countless particles
mission-011.scientificFact: Saturn is not the only planet with rings, but it has the broadest and most easily observed ring system in the Solar System.

dossier.overview: Cross-referencing clues makes it possible to identify bodies without revealing their names. Saturn combines low average density, gaseous composition and an exceptional ring system.
sections: Structural evidence
It is composed mainly of hydrogen and helium and has no defined solid surface.
Orbital evidence
Ice and rock particles form numerous rings and divisions.
Scientific method
A reliable identification uses several clues instead of relying on a generic characteristic.
dossier.learnMore: Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune also have rings. Combining appearance, composition, density, moons and orbital properties makes identification more rigorous.

mission-012.title: Earth's memory
mission-012.description: begin the lunar campaign by investigating Earth's only natural satellite and the records preserved on its surface.

questions.question: Why can footprints from the Apollo missions remain on the Moon for so long?
alternatives: Because the Moon produces a protective resin
Because there is almost no atmosphere, wind or rain
Because they are under a layer of water

questions.question: Which important effect does the Moon's gravity have on Earth?

scanData: Atmosphere: extremely tenuous exosphere
Surface: craters, basaltic maria and regolith
Orbit: about 27.3 days around Earth
mission-012.scientificFact: The Moon helps stabilize the tilt of Earth's axis and strongly influences the tides.

dossier.overview: The Moon preserves billions of years of impacts and volcanism. Without a dense atmosphere or flowing water, its surface changes slowly.
sections: Environment
Extreme temperatures, almost no air and direct exposure to radiation characterize the surface.
Orbit
Its synchronous rotation means that we almost always see the same side.
Exploration
It was the first body beyond Earth visited in person by human beings.
dossier.learnMore: The lunar maria contain no water: they are extensive plains of solidified lava. Water ice has been detected in permanently shadowed regions near the poles.

mission-013.title: The ocean beneath the ice
mission-013.description: the sensors indicate a young, fractured crust concealing a possible global ocean in the Jupiter system.

questions.question: Which evidence makes Europa an important target in the search for habitable environments?
alternatives: A possible salty ocean beneath the ice crust
An atmosphere rich in breathable oxygen

questions.question: Which process helps keep Europa's interior warm?
alternatives: Tidal heating caused by Jupiter's gravity

scanData: Crust: fractured and relatively young ice
Interior: strong evidence of a salty ocean
Energy: heating by tidal forces
mission-013.scientificFact: Europa's ocean may contain more liquid water than all of Earth's oceans combined.

dossier.overview: Europa is an icy moon of Jupiter. Magnetic measurements and its fractured surface support the hypothesis of a global subsurface ocean.
sections: Surface
Bright ice, grooves and few craters suggest geological renewal.
Interior
The ocean probably lies between the crust and a rocky mantle.
Astrobiology
Liquid water, chemistry and energy make Europa a priority target.
dossier.learnMore: The gravity of Jupiter and neighboring moons repeatedly deforms Europa. This friction releases heat and may sustain liquid water far from sunlight.

mission-014.title: The world of fire
mission-014.description: investigate the most volcanically active known moon, marked by plumes and a constantly renewed surface.

questions.question: What powers Io's extreme volcanism?
Why does Io have relatively few visible impact craters?
alternatives: Volcanism renews and covers the surface
Craters occur only on the hidden side

scanData: Activity: hundreds of volcanic centers
Surface: sulfur compounds and lava
Heat source: continuous gravitational deformation
mission-014.scientificFact: Some of Io's volcanic plumes rise hundreds of kilometers above the surface.

dossier.overview: Io is compressed and stretched by Jupiter's gravity and by orbital resonance with Europa and Ganymede.
sections: Volcanism
Lava lakes, plumes and extensive flows reshape the moon.
Composition
Sulfur and sulfur dioxide produce yellow, red and white tones.
Orbit
Eccentricity maintained by neighboring moons sustains internal heating.
dossier.learnMore: Io acts as a natural laboratory for tidal heating. Escaping material also supplies a plasma torus around Jupiter.

mission-015.title: Larger than Mercury
mission-015.description: find the largest moon in the Solar System and analyze a magnetic property unique among natural satellites.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes Ganymede's size?
alternatives: It is smaller than all of Mars's moons
It is larger in diameter than Mercury
It has the same diameter as the Moon

questions.question: Which feature makes Ganymede unique among known moons?
alternatives: It has its own magnetic field

scanData: Diameter: approximately 5,268 km
Structure: rock, ice and a probable internal ocean
Magnetism: intrinsic magnetic field
mission-015.scientificFact: Ganymede is larger than Mercury, although it has only about half its mass.

dossier.overview: Ganymede combines planetary dimensions, an icy surface, a probable subsurface ocean and its own magnetic field.
sections: Dimensions
It is the largest moon in the Solar System, with a diameter greater than Mercury's but much less mass.
Surface
Ancient dark terrain exists alongside brighter, grooved regions.
Interior
A metallic core helps generate its magnetosphere.
dossier.learnMore: Ganymede's magnetic field creates a small magnetosphere inside Jupiter's enormous magnetosphere. Auroras help scientists study its interior.

mission-016.title: Methane rivers
mission-016.description: cross the orange haze of a moon with a thick atmosphere, lakes and hydrocarbon rain.

questions.question: Which substances form much of the lakes and seas on Titan's surface?
Which gas dominates Titan's atmosphere?

scanData: Atmosphere: dense and dominated by nitrogen
Surface: lakes and channels of methane and ethane
Temperature: about −179 °C
mission-016.scientificFact: Titan is the only known world beyond Earth with stable liquids forming lakes and seas on its surface.

dossier.overview: Titan has weather, clouds, rain, rivers and seas, but its meteorological cycle uses methane instead of water.
sections: Atmosphere
Nitrogen and an organic haze conceal the surface in visible light.
Climate
Methane evaporates, forms clouds, precipitates and returns to the seas.
Exploration
The Huygens probe landed on Titan in 2005 and transmitted data from the surface.
dossier.learnMore: Beneath its icy crust, Titan probably also harbors an ocean of water. Its organic chemistry is relevant to research on processes that precede life.

mission-017.title: Geysers in the void
mission-017.description: analyze jets of ice and vapor that make it possible to study a hidden ocean without drilling through the surface.

questions.question: Where do the plumes observed at Enceladus's south pole come from?
Why do the plumes make Enceladus's ocean easier to study?
alternatives: They carry internal material into space, where it can be analyzed

scanData: South pole: fractures called tiger stripes
Plumes: vapor, ice, salts and organic molecules
Interior: global ocean beneath the crust
mission-017.scientificFact: Particles ejected by Enceladus help form Saturn's E ring.

dossier.overview: Enceladus is small, bright and geologically active. Its jets directly expose samples from a subsurface ocean.
sections: Plumes
Jets escape through heated fractures in the south polar region.
Ocean
Liquid water interacts with a rocky seafloor, creating interesting chemical possibilities.
Habitability
Water, salts, organic compounds and energy have been detected.
dossier.learnMore: Cassini flew through the plumes and analyzed their particles. Evidence of hydrothermal activity suggests reactions between hot water and rock on the ocean floor.

mission-018.title: The backward orbit
mission-018.description: conclude the campaign by investigating an icy moon traveling in a retrograde orbit around Neptune.

questions.question: What does it mean to say that Triton has a retrograde orbit?
alternatives: It orbits in the direction opposite to Neptune's rotation

questions.question: Which hypothesis best explains Triton's unusual orbit?
alternatives: It was gravitationally captured by Neptune
It is a fragment of Earth
It was built by the rings

scanData: Orbit: retrograde and highly inclined
Surface: nitrogen, methane and water ices
Activity: dark geysers observed by Voyager 2
mission-018.scientificFact: Its retrograde orbit indicates that Triton probably formed in the Kuiper Belt and was captured by Neptune.

dossier.overview: Triton is Neptune's largest moon and combines a young surface, a tenuous atmosphere and an orbit that reveals an external origin.
sections: Orbit
It moves in the direction opposite to the planet's rotation, which is rare for a large moon.
Surface
It is one of the coldest known surfaces, covered by volatile ices.
Evolution
Tidal interaction causes Triton to slowly approach Neptune.
dossier.learnMore: In the distant future, Triton may cross the Roche limit and break apart, perhaps forming a new ring system around Neptune.

mission-019.title: Guardian of the belt
mission-019.description: begin the bonus investigations by finding the largest body in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
mission-019.objective: Find Ceres in the asteroid belt.

questions.question: Where is the main asteroid belt concentrated?
Why is Ceres classified as a dwarf planet?
alternatives: Because it does not orbit the Sun
Because it is only a cloud of gas
Because it is nearly spherical but has not cleared its orbital neighborhood
Because it has more mass than Jupiter

scanData: Location: main belt between Mars and Jupiter
Diameter: approximately 946 km
Composition: rock, ice and hydrated minerals
mission-019.scientificFact: Ceres contains about one third of the estimated mass of the entire main asteroid belt.

dossier.overview: Ceres is the largest body in the main belt and the only dwarf planet located in the inner Solar System.
sections: Asteroid belt
The region contains millions of bodies, but they are separated by great distances.
Classification
Ceres orbits the Sun and is nearly spherical, but shares its orbital region with many objects.
Exploration
The Dawn spacecraft revealed craters, bright salt deposits and signs of geological activity.
dossier.learnMore: The belt is not a compact barrier like those shown in movies. Its total mass is small, and distances between objects are generally enormous.

mission-020.title: Beyond Neptune
mission-020.description: travel to the Kuiper Belt to investigate an icy world with mountains, plains and five known moons.

questions.question: In which region of the Solar System is Pluto located?
Which requirement does Pluto not meet to be classified as a major planet?
alternatives: Having cleared the neighborhood of its orbit

scanData: Orbit: beyond Neptune, eccentric and inclined
Surface: nitrogen, methane and carbon monoxide ices
System: five known moons, including Charon
mission-020.scientificFact: The New Horizons mission revealed ice mountains and a vast heart-shaped plain on Pluto.

dossier.overview: Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, a region populated by icy bodies left over from the formation of the Solar System.
sections: Surface
Volatile ices form plains, mountains and surprisingly young terrain.
Orbit
Its path is more inclined and eccentric than those of the eight planets.
Classification
It shares its orbital zone with many Kuiper Belt objects.
dossier.learnMore: Pluto and Charon orbit a center of mass located outside Pluto. For this reason, the system is sometimes informally described as a double dwarf planet.

mission-021.title: Messenger of ice
mission-021.description: complete the bonus archive by following a periodic comet that crosses the inner and outer regions of the Solar System.
mission-021.objective: Find Halley's Comet in its elongated orbit.

questions.question: Why does a comet's tail generally point away from the Sun?
alternatives: Because the comet always travels backward
Because of solar radiation and the solar wind
Because the tail is a shadow

questions.question: What does a highly elongated orbit cause the comet to experience?
alternatives: The same distance from the Sun throughout its path
Large changes in distance and heating

scanData: Nucleus: dark mixture of ice, dust and rock
Orbit: highly eccentric and retrograde
Period: approximately 75 to 76 years
mission-021.scientificFact: Halley's Comet was the first comet recognized as periodic; its next passage through the inner Solar System will occur in 2061.

dossier.overview: Halley's Comet periodically visits the inner Solar System. As it warms, it releases gas and dust that form a coma and tails.
sections: Nucleus
Ices mixed with dust remain relatively inactive far from the Sun.
Activity
Solar heating sublimates the ices and creates a temporary atmosphere around the nucleus.
Tails
Radiation and the solar wind push particles and gases away from the Sun.
dossier.learnMore: A comet may display a curved dust tail and a straighter ion tail. Their directions depend on the Sun, not necessarily on the comet's direction of travel.
